name: apple-mail-mcp
description: Search and read macOS Mail, and send messages you approve. Never deletes or moves anything.
long_description:
A local MCP server written in Swift that gives Claude access to the Mail app on this Mac.

Mail has no framework a separate process can use, so this server drives Mail.app through Apple events. Mail must be running, and Mail — not this server — is what reads the mailbox. That makes every query slow, so a search always stops after a fixed number of messages or a fixed time rather than crawling every mailbox of every account, and says so plainly when it had to stop early.

Results come in pages. A search returns a page of messages and a message is read through a window of its text; whenever more exists than a result holds, its first lines say how much there is and the exact argument that returns the rest.

The permission is Automation, granted per target app. macOS asks the first time a tool contacts Mail, and the grant appears under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Automation.

Plug and play: there is nothing to configure.

Nothing here can delete, move or alter a received message. Mail's scripting dictionary offers those commands and they are deliberately not exposed: a mailbox is a record.

send_mail is the only outward-facing tool and it cannot be undone — no recall, no undo. It requires an explicit confirmation, checks every address first, and returns a receipt naming every recipient list including bcc. Switch it off below if you only want Claude to read.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple Inc.

tools.name: mail_status
tools.description: Report whether Mail is running and automation is permitted, and the fixed sizes in force. Reads no mail.

tools.name: mail_accounts
tools.description: List accounts, mailboxes and unread counts, a page at a time

tools.name: mail_search
tools.description: Find messages by sender or subject, bounded by mailbox and date, a page at a time

tools.name: mail_get
tools.description: Read one message, a window of its text at a time. Does not mark it as read.

tools.name: send_mail
tools.description: Send an email. Cannot be undone; requires explicit confirmation.
